title: Perception: Hearing - Place Theory, Frequency Theory
summary: Place theory of hearing; frequency theory of hearing; auditory perception mechanisms.
objectives: Explain which frequencies each theory explains best.
revision: Place theory = different places on basilar membrane for different frequencies (high at base, low at apex). Frequency theory = neural firing rate matches sound frequency (low frequencies).
traps: Frequency theory = low frequencies (firing rate matches sound wave).
confusions: Confusing place theory (place on membrane) with frequency theory (firing rate).
Believing one theory explains all frequencies.

notes.t: Place theory proposes that different sound frequencies stimulate different places along the basilar membrane in the cochlea. High frequencies at the base, low frequencies at the apex.
Frequency theory proposes that the rate of neural impulses matches the frequency of the sound wave, explaining perception of low-frequency sounds.
Place theory explains high-frequency perception; frequency theory explains low-frequency perception. Modern understanding combines both (volley principle for intermediate frequencies).
UGC NET frequently asks to contrast place theory (high frequency) with frequency theory (low frequency) of hearing.

mnemonics.title: PF
mnemonics.text: P — Place theory (high frequency, basilar membrane place), F — Frequency theory (low frequency, neural firing rate)

flashcards.a: Different frequencies stimulate different places on basilar membrane.
Neural firing rate matches sound frequency (low frequencies).
